title: bug: ignore patterns in ls tool do not work for path-relative/nested globs

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue clearly describes a specific bug in ls.ts where ignore patterns fail for path-relative/nested globs due to passing only the file basename to shouldIgnore and using a naive regex replacement. Code locations and clear expected behavior are provided.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: The fix is localized to a single source file (packages/core/src/tools/ls.ts) and its unit test. It involves replacing the custom regex logic with picomatch and evaluating relative paths.

summary.problem: The ls tool ignore parameter does not work for path-relative or nested glob patterns because entries are evaluated against only their basename using a naive regex converter.
summary.root_cause: In packages/core/src/tools/ls.ts, shouldIgnore converts globs using simple string replacement and tests only path.basename(fullPath).
summary.context: picomatch is already present as a dependency in packages/core. Replacing the custom regex with picomatch and evaluating relative paths resolves the issue.

steps: Refactor LSToolInvocation.shouldIgnore to utilize picomatch for pattern matching with options dot: true and matchBase: true.
Update the execution loop in LSToolInvocation.execute to check relative paths against shouldIgnore rather than only path.basename(fullPath).

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: ls tool successfully filters out files when ignore patterns contain path separators or nested glob wildcards (e.g., 'subdir/*.txt' or 'nested/**/ignore.log').
verification_steps: Add test cases in packages/core/src/tools/ls.test.ts for nested ignore patterns such as 'subdir/*.txt' and '**/ignored.log'.
Run Vitest on packages/core/src/tools/ls.test.ts to verify all tests pass.
